claims.text: CodePipeline's default execution mode is `SUPERSEDED`.
In CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode, a stage is locked to one execution at a time.
In CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` mode, a newer execution can overtake an older execution that is still waiting to enter a locked stage, dropping the waiting execution before it starts.
If a CodeBuild stage running `pulumi up` is busy and enough commits land, a queued CodePipeline execution waiting behind it can be superseded and never run, silently skipping a deployment.
Setting a CodePipeline pipeline's execution mode to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions form a queue and each runs in turn.
CodePipeline's `QUEUED` execution mode requires a V2 pipeline type.
The AWS CLI's `create-pipeline` and `update-pipeline` commands accept `executionMode` and `pipelineType` settings for a pipeline.
The Pulumi `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` resource has `executionMode` and `pipelineType` inputs.
The Pulumi Registry page for `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` exists at /registry/packages/aws/api-docs/codepipeline/pipeline/ and the pipeline resource is described below in the page.
When two runs reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them, and the other run's `pulumi up` fails with an update conflict.
Azure Pipelines supports an exclusive lock check on an environment, which can be applied to the environment targeted by a deployment job to prevent concurrent runs.
In Azure DevOps, an exclusive lock check is added from the environment's 'Approvals and checks' tab.
In Azure Pipelines YAML, `lockBehavior` is a stage-level property that is set on the stage referencing the environment with the exclusive lock check.
The default value of Azure Pipelines `lockBehavior` is `runLatest`.
With `lockBehavior: runLatest`, only the most recently queued run acquires the exclusive lock, and older runs waiting behind it are passed over (cancelled) rather than eventually applied.
With `lockBehavior: sequential`, every queued stage run acquires the exclusive lock in order, one at a time.
Pulumi Cloud serializes updates to a stack, one at a time in order.
The `azuredevops.CheckExclusiveLock` resource exists in the Azure DevOps provider in the Pulumi Registry and manages the exclusive lock check as code.
The `Pulumi@1` Azure Pipelines task accepts inputs `command`, `stack`, and `args`, with `command: up` and `args: --yes`.
Link targets exist: /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ and /registry/packages/azuredevops/api-docs/checkexclusivelock/, and the Microsoft approvals docs page.
When two runs of the same build configuration reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them.
When two runs reach the same stack concurrently, the second run's `pulumi up` fails with an update conflict error.
TeamCity's default is to let build configurations run concurrently against as many free agents as are available.
The page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ exists and documents update conflicts.
TeamCity's build configuration advanced option 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' is located under the configuration's General Settings.
The TeamCity option 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' defaults to 0, meaning unlimited.
Setting TeamCity's 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' to 1 causes a second build to be queued and run only after the first finishes.
Pulumi Cloud has a per-stack lease that gives one-at-a-time update behavior.
In Azure Pipelines, adding an exclusive lock check to the environment targeted by a deployment job serializes deployments to that environment.
In Azure Pipelines YAML, the stage-level setting `lockBehavior: sequential` makes runs queue sequentially when an exclusive lock check is used.
The page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/azure-devops/ has a section anchored at #serialize-deployments-with-an-exclusive-lock.
AWS CodePipeline pipelines have an execution mode setting that can be set to `QUEUED`, in which waiting executions run in turn.
In AWS CodePipeline, the default execution mode (SUPERSEDED) lets a newer execution supersede an older one that is still waiting to start.
The page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/aws-code-services/ has a section anchored at #serialize-pipeline-executions.
In TeamCity, the build configuration setting 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' set to 1 restricts the configuration to one running build at a time.
The page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/teamcity/ has a section anchored at #limit-concurrent-builds.
